All-New 2028 Cadillac Escalade PHEV Gains Deep Facelift Along With Plug-in Hybrid Setup – Rendering
21 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
General Motors has recently announced that it is looking forward to engineering the “intelligence-defined vehicle for everyone,” as GM is joining the pack of automakers that are seeking “a fundamental transformation of our vehicles” as we know them.
GM will focus on a combination of AI, software-defined platforms, intelligent manufacturing, and trusted autonomous systems, with Cadillac at the forefront of the activities, of course. The premium brand needs attention, as sales have suffered because of its over-reliance on EVs, and the parent company now wants to help it gain back on the right course, with no expenses spared.
Even the OnStar service is going to be morphed into an AI assistant for the GM cars, especially Cadillacs at first, and the luxury brand is currently focused on its most popular model with ICE power in a bid to draw attention. For example, F1 driver Checo Perez got his own Escalade-V special edition, limited to just 11 examples, while the company also created the Escalade 125th Anniversary Collector Series with exclusive wheels, carbon fiber, and blue accents, among other things.
As such, perhaps it’s no surprise that even the rumor mill, along with the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, have thoughts about Cadillac in general and also about the Escalade in particular. More precisely, here are the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube who have recently and unofficially imagined the CGI look of the potential all-new 2028 Cadillac Escalade PHEV for the US market.
The channel’s host believes that the upcoming sixth generation of the Cadillac Escalade might arrive in 2027 or 2028 because the current iteration has been around since 2020 and a mid-cycle refresh procedure was applied in 2024 for the 2025 model year. However, do take their assessment with a pinch of salt because Cadillac might simply apply a second refresh if they want to bring to market new features along with the fresh powertrain.
Speaking of the latter, the host believes that Cadillac will offer the first-ever plug-in hybrid powertrain based on a 1.5-liter four-cylinder turbo helped by two electric motors. However, that’s also rather unlikely, as GM won’t de-escalate the value of an Escalade with a four-cylinder. Instead, it would be plausible that one of the new V8 engines from the 2027 Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra, the 5.7-liter or the 6.6-liter, could get an electrified setup to keep the Escalade’s elegance and power uncompromised.
Last but not least, the channel’s resident virtual artist quickly takes over to present the potential changes featured on the 2028 Cadillac Escalade PHEV, starting with a quick comparison with the current model to showcase the new visual identity, which includes a new front fascia and a reworked interior. Last but not least, they don’t forget about the traditional CGI color reel. So, what do you think – yay or nay?
